propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Custodi, Domine, quaesumus, Ecclesiam tuam propitiatione perpetua: et quia
sine te labitur humana mortalitas; tuis semper auxiliis et abstrahatur a
noxiis, et ad salutaria dirigatur. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 425 under `COLLECT. Custodi.` after the Introit `Protector noster` of the formulary headed `XIV. SUNDAY after PENTECOST.`. The printed Latin cue Custodi. and the English petition answer the target Custodi, Domine. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked. This is the pre-1955 lay hand-missal English witness, not a modern approved liturgical translation.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: Preserve, O Lord, we beseech thee, thy Church by thy constant mercy: and since our weak mortality is continually falling without thy assistance, may thy grace withdraw it from what is hurtful, and direct it in the ways of salvation. Thro'.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Concede nobis, Domine, quaesumus, ut haec hostia salutaris, et nostrorum
fiat purgatio delictorum, et tuae propitiatio potestatis. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 427 (running head `XV. SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST.`) under `SECRET.—` with no Latin cue, after the Fourteenth Sunday's Offertory `Ps. xxxiii.` and before the heading `XV. SUNDAY after PENTECOST.`. Its position before the Communion within Sunday XIV and the clauses for the saving victim, cleansing sins and divine favour answer Concede nobis, Domine ... hostia salutaris ... purgatio delictorum ... propitiatio potestatis. translations.text: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, that this victim of salvation may both cleanse us from our sins, and render thy Majesty propitious to us. Thro'.
